data.title: 4 stocks to watch on Friday: JBLU, MDB, SKHY, and AVGO
data.description:
Stock index futures were higher on Friday, a day after a rebound in Treasury yields triggered a sell-off on Wall Street on Thursday.

Here are four stocks to watch on the day: 

JetBlue (JBLU) rose 1.27% after Carl Icahn lowered his active stake in the airline to 3.3% following the sale of more shares. Icahn and associated entities reported owning 12,528,346 shares, taking the stake below the 5% threshold for SEC reporting requirements. Icahn remained the airline’s largest shareholder outside asset managers such as BlackRock and Vanguard.

MongoDB (MDB) rose 1.10% after Evercore initiated coverage with an Outperform rating and a $525 price target. Analyst Kirk Materne highlighted strong developer adoption, a flexible data model, and growing enterprise use. Atlas, MongoDB’s cloud offering, accounted for roughly 75% of revenue and was becoming increasingly relevant for AI workloads.

SK Hynix (SKHY) gained 2.58% as the South Korean memory-chip maker considered building a manufacturing plant in Japan’s Miyagi prefecture. The potential project could involve an investment of tens of trillions of won, according to Japanese media reports. The expansion would target rising global memory chip demand, particularly from AI infrastructure.

Broadcom (AVGO) gained 1.3% amid reports that it was in talks with Blackstone and Apollo Global Management to raise more than $60B in debt. The financing would support AI infrastructure tied to Anthropic, according to Bloomberg. The deal could include a $30B junior debt tranche and a senior-secured tranche, with Broadcom likely securing part of the latter.

data.title: Citi sees pre-midterm weakness as a buying opportunity
data.description:
Citigroup remained overweight equities and suggested adding exposure if markets pulled back ahead of the U.S. midterm elections, according to Walter Bloomberg.

Citi pointed to supportive earnings revisions, improving liquidity conditions, and limited warning signs despite recent concerns around AI. The bank continued to favor U.S. stocks while arguing that sector rotation could help limit downside.

Historically, pre-midterm market weakness had often been followed by strong year-end performance, according to the post. That history suggested any pullback ahead of the elections could present an opportunity for investors to add to equity exposure.

The bank's view was that the broader market backdrop remained supportive, with earnings and liquidity providing a cushion even as investors remained focused on AI-related concerns.

data.title: Fifth Third Bancorp begins exchange offer for unregistered senior notes
data.description:
Fifth Third Bancorp (FITB) on Friday said it has commenced an offer to exchange outstanding unregistered senior notes for an equal principal amount of new registered notes.

The terms are substantially identical to the terms of the restricted notes offering completed on June 10.

data.title: Carl Icahn lowers his stake in JetBlue below the reporting threshold
data.description:
Carl Icahn lowered his active stake in JetBlue Airways Corporation (JBLU) to 3.3% following the sale of more shares. In an SEC filing, Icahn and his associated entities reported that they owned 12,528,346 shares of JetBlue (JBLU) common stock. The filing noted that as a result of the recent transactions, the reporting persons ceased to be beneficial owners of more than 5% of JetBlue's (JBLU) common stock and are no longer subject to the reporting requirements of the SEC's Rule 13d-1(a).

Despite the reduction of Icahn's stake in the airline company, he is still the largest holder of shares that is not an asset manager such as BlackRock (BLK) or Vanguard.

Icahn began buying JetBlue (JBLUE) shares in January of 2024, building a position for what he said was an "attractive investment opportunity." His stake went as high as 9.9%, and he landed two of his representatives on the JetBlue (JBLU) board.

Shares of JetBlue (JBLU) were up 1.3% in premarket trading on Friday to $4.80 vs. the 52-week range of $3.87 to $6.62. Short interest on JBLU stands at 25.3% of the total float.

data.title: More Brazilian cities join Vale-BHP dam collapse payout deal
data.description:
The compensation agreement with miners Vale (VALE), BHP (BHP), and the Samarco joint venture for the 2015 tailings dam collapse in Mariana has been joined by 19 new cities, ​including the city that was at the epicenter of the disaster, bringing the total to 45 of 49 eligible municipalities, a Brazilian ‌court said Thursday.

The agreement ​signed in 2024 established the payment of 170B reais (~$32.7B) in compensation and reparation for one of Brazil's worst environmental disasters, with 6B reais earmarked for affected cities.

Cities have been slow to join the deal, however, arguing that 170B reais was not enough to compensate for the vast damage, and the initial resistance was also influenced by parallel legal action against BHP (BHP) in London, which also seeks reparations ‌for ⁠the collapse that could yield an even higher compensation amount.

London's High Court ruled last November that BHP (BHP) was responsible under Brazilian law for the dam collapse; a further trial to decide on any damages to be paid is expected to begin in April 2027.

data.title: Australia's Steadfast to be acquired by KKR-led group for $5.5B
data.description:
An investor group led by affiliates of KKR (KKR) and Dragoneer Investment Group, plus Amwins Group, agreed to acquire Australian insurance company Steadfast Group (SFGLF) for ~A$7.7B (US$5.5B), the company said in a filing on Friday.

Under the terms of the agreement, Steadfast shareholders will get A$6.00 per share in cash, less the cash amount of any permitted dividends paid per Steadfast share. The price represents a 51.9% premium to the stock's unaffected price of A$3.95 on June 9, 2026, the last trading day before the news that Steadfast had received a proposal from Dragoneer and Amwins.

With the completion of the deal, Amwins Australasia will acquire Steadfast's underwriting agency, and the investor group will own Steadfast's broking business. The transaction is expected to be completed in mid- to late December, the companies said in the filing.

data.title: Blue Ant Media expands share buyback program
data.description:
• Blue Ant Media (BAMI:CA)  said it will increase the size of its normal course issuer bid to 1.81M subordinate voting shares from 1.09M, effective Aug. 25.
  • The company will also raise its daily repurchase limit to 7,582 shares from 1,000. Blue Ant had repurchased 108,300 shares under the program as of July 31.

data.title: Taming bond yields: What else can Bessent pull out of the Treasury toolkit?
data.description:
It's been quite a few days for the U.S. bond market, with investors still sizing up the latest fallout and where things may go from here. Under the direction of Secretary Scott Bessent, the U.S. Treasury on Wednesday announced that it would double its buybacks to serve as a backstop for longer-maturity government bonds (a.k.a. preventing the 30-year Treasury yield from continuing its upward trajectory). While the maneuver initially knocked the 30-year yield (US30Y) down 10 basis points to 5.19%, the relief was short-lived as yields quickly resumed their climb back to 5.26% during trading on Thursday.

What's at play? There's been a debate surrounding why yields are rising, as well as what to do about it—if anything. Note that yields have been on the march higher for years, but more recently, concerns over government debt, the amount of corporate issuance, poor liquidity, or plain old vigilantism might be to blame. It's a reason for concern. Higher bond yields mean that the Treasury is locking in higher borrowing costs, which can translate into even larger deficits barring some serious economic growth. As a result, the U.S. Treasury is figuring out its options, while some warn that any intervention won't change the fundamentals and to leave market forces alone.

"We have a big toolkit, so we'll see. And part of it is signaling here," Bessent declared, unveiling a twist operation of buying back longer-dated bonds with cash raised from short-term sales. While this is a routine operational mechanism, there are concerns here for the dollar, or should the program be prolonged or increase in size. "Governments trying to control markets is not a particularly attractive story most of the time," noted JPMorgan's James Sullivan. "It's a little bit like paying your mortgage with your credit card. It can work for a while, but eventually the mismatch becomes more obvious."

Outlook: What else can the Treasury do to cap yields and keep bond volatility out of the headlines? Bessent's $4B buyback target is tiny a faction of the the total $32T Treasury market, so the program could be ramped up even further. Bessent is also planning an upcoming press conference to discuss fiscal consolidation, but other immediate ideas may include cutting down the issuance of longer-dated debt or altering bank capital rules to boost demand. In case of an emergency, the U.S. Treasury could coordinate with the Federal Reserve on the yield curve, its balance-sheet runoff, or global central banks on joint interventions to reduce foreign selling pressure on U.S. debt.
